name: TransDigm
description: TransDigm designs and makes proprietary aircraft parts (actuators, latches, valves, power and cabin components) through many separate operating units. A part is engineered into an aircraft once and then sold as a replacement for the 25 to 30 years the plane flies. About 55% of FY2025 sales came from the aftermarket, which the 10-K says earns higher gross profit and is more stable than sales to aircraft builders. Sales split roughly 30-35% commercial aftermarket, 25-30% commercial OEM and 35-40% defense. The company reports profit as EBITDA As Defined and runs a 53.9% margin on that measure, financed with heavy debt ($33.5B) and negative stockholders' equity of $9.8B, funding acquisitions, occasional large special dividends and buybacks. In April 2026 it bought Jet Parts Engineering and Victor Sierra for about $2.2B, adding makers of FAA-approved replacement (PMA) parts that are alternatives to original manufacturers' parts.

businessLines.name: Power & Control
businessLines.how: Proprietary parts: sold to aircraft builders at the start, then to airlines, repair shops and militaries as replacements over decades; the 10-K says aftermarket sales earn higher gross profit than OEM sales.
businessLines.description: Systems and components that supply or control power on the aircraft: mechanical/electromechanical actuators, pumps, valves, ignition, electronics. JPE and VSA (April 2026) are included here.

businessLines.name: Airframe
businessLines.how: Same proprietary-aftermarket model as Power & Control, applied to airframe and cabin parts.
businessLines.description: Non-power airframe and cabin components: latching and locking devices, engineered rods and connectors, seating and cabin structures, audio and lighting.

businessLines.name: Non-aviation
businessLines.how: Product sales into non-aviation markets; a small segment and the lowest margin.
businessLines.description: Seat belts and restraints for ground vehicles, space actuators and controls, and other non-aviation industrial products.
